caption: A dog lying in a hallway jumps up as a lightning flash lights the windows and the house shakes with thunder.

sa.check: A dog lies in a hallway.
A lightning flash lights the windows.
A window or windows are in view in the hallway.
The flash comes first and the dog jumps after it.

pc.expect: The flash is brief: the windows and the hallway brighten and return to their earlier light; flashes may repeat but each ends.
pc.fail: The hallway stays bright to the end of the clip after the flash; or brightens steadily without ending; or the flash fades in slowly; or the windows stay lit while the hallway is dark again.

pc.expect: The light enters through the windows: the windows are the brightest part, the walls and floor near them brighten most, and shadows of the frames fall away from the windows during the flash.
pc.fail: The hallway brightens evenly while the windows stay as they were; or the light comes from the far end of the hallway with the windows dark; or the window frames' shadows point toward the windows.

pc.expect: The flash moves nothing but the dog: furniture, pictures, doors and rugs stay put.
pc.fail: Pictures, furniture or doors shift at the flash; or the rug slides; or the dog is lifted off the floor without its legs pushing.

pc.expect: The dog rises by pushing off with its legs and lands back on the floor, its body moving as one animal.
pc.fail: The dog rises straight up and hangs in the air; or slides across the floor without its legs moving; or lands and slides on with nothing pushing it.

pc.expect: One dog with the same body, legs and tail throughout; the hallway's walls, doors and windows keep their shape and nothing passes through anything.
pc.fail: The dog gains or loses a leg or its head changes shape; or a second dog appears; or the dog passes through a wall or door; or a window changes shape or moves along the wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The dog's coat colour, the wall colours and the pictures stay the same apart from brightness.
pc.fail: The dog's coat changes colour or pattern; or the walls change colour; or pictures on the wall change.

note: The dog is kept because its reaction is the caption's event; a dog starting to move is not causeless motion. Thunder is sound and the house 'shaking' is not judged.
